findings.reason: this sentence is the specification for the per-section predicate an implementer will write, so a cited field that does not resolve either reads `None` and silently answers "not held", or sends the implementer to the wrong reader, and no arm in §8 exercises a plan-level `blocking` row to catch it.
findings.text: §8 names "the plan-level `gate_blockers` and `blocking`" as roadmap fields that report a section's holds, but the roadmap row built at `reckon/roadmap.py:3488` carries no `blocking` key: `blocking` is the authored plan-state list read only as `plan.get("blocking")` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3367-3375`), whose `explicit` and `held` rows surface on the row as `explicit_blockers` and `held_blockers`, and all of them are plan-level holds that name no section

findings.reason: without the gate-held arm in the gate, an implementer who satisfies "the shared assembly exposes one per-section predicate" by wrapping the existing `section_holds_by_plan` passes every arm and launches a request whose section the plan's own gate holds, which is the exact failure the changed paragraph was written to correct.
findings.text: the mechanism paragraph requires "Tests cover a section held by its plan's gate both when other implementable sections are not named by that gate and when every implementable section is, and in both cases the waiter stays `awaiting-upstream`", but §8's done-when names no gate-held arm; the roadmap already exposes a per-section hold map, `section_holds_by_plan` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3638-3653`), and it is empty for the second shape because `named_holds` reads only `section_gate_blockers`, which `split_unpassed_gates` returns empty once every implementable section is named by an open gate (`reckon/roadmap.py:898-901`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the paragraph lists the plan-level `blocking` as a roadmap hold field, but no such key exists on a roadmap row or on `build_roadmap`'s report; every other citation resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's done-when has no arm for a section held by its plan's gate, so the crux of the paragraph that just changed is measured only by a sentence in the mechanism prose.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8 writes only in-repo modules (`queue_admission.py`, `dispatch_admission.py`, `crew_dispatch_commands.py`, `node.py`, `plan_review.py`) and a new test file, and names no scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols named (`RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES`, the two wait-phase states, the per-section predicate) are mechanism names; no plan label, ticket or version tag reaches code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the root cause matches the cited evidence (`parse_manifest` really refuses `completed`/`done`/`landed`/`promoted`, since `MANIFEST_STATUSES` is `TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES | NON_TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES | {"waiting","derived"}` and the non-terminal set is `{"in-progress","in_progress","running","pending"}`), the mechanism produces the done-when arms, and the caller is named by §2's `admit_once`, whose `advance_waiting_requests` builds the per-pass cache the paragraph describes.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable: a request's waits are the union of its section's refs, its plan's `depends_on`, its gates and `--after` refs, resolved per section across plans and projects.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s8's only declared edge (`s2`) is the section that adds `awaiting-upstream`, the readiness re-read and `_readiness_rows`, which §8's mechanism builds on; s9 and s15 each declare their dependence on s8 and the relationship points the right way.
